    Common questions

    Quick answers

    Straight answers to the questions customers ask first. The full list is on our FAQ page.

    Does the price include delivery?

    Guide prices on our Sizes & Prices page exclude delivery and tax. Your quote is different: it's one all-in delivered price for your site, with delivery and HST (15% in PEI) worked out per job, because both depend on where the container lands.

    Which size should I get — 20ft or 40ft?

    A 20ft is the standard job-site and farm choice and fits tighter sites. A 40ft high-cube gives you roughly double the volume and extra ceiling height for not much more money, if your site has the room. Tell us what you're storing and we'll steer you right — including telling you if the smaller unit is enough.

    What's the difference between used, cargo-worthy, and one-trip?

    Used wind & watertight units seal out weather and are the best value for storage. Cargo-worthy units are certified sound enough to ship cargo by sea. One-trip units have made a single loaded trip, so they're near-new inside and out. Our Services page explains each grade in plain language.

    Conditions explained

    Know what you're buying

    Container grades, in plain language — so the unit that arrives matches what you expected.

    Wind & watertight (used)

    A retired shipping container that still seals out wind and rain. Surface rust and dents are normal. The workhorse choice for storage — and the best value per square foot.

    Cargo-worthy (used)

    A used unit certified sound enough to ship cargo by sea. Structurally stronger than a basic storage grade — the grade to ask for if the container itself is travelling.

    One-trip (near-new)

    A container that has made a single loaded trip from the factory. Minimal wear, clean interior, current colours — the closest thing to new, for sites where appearance matters.

    Before the truck arrives

    Getting your site ready

    A few practical things that make delivery day smooth.

    • Clear, level ground. A tilt-bed truck needs a firm, reasonably level spot and room to tilt and slide the container off. Soft or sloped ground can need blocks or gravel — tell us about your site when you ask for a quote.

    • Check your local rules first. Charlottetown restricts storage containers on residential lots, and nearby municipalities allow them only as temporary ~60-day storage. Ask us and we'll help you check before you commit.

    • Winter weather can move a date. The Confederation Bridge closes to high-sided vehicles 8–12 times a winter for wind. If your delivery is booked on one of those days, we'll reschedule at no extra charge.

    • Delivered prices are quoted per job. Distance, site access, and the Confederation Bridge crossing all move the number — which is exactly why we quote one all-in price instead of posting a delivery chart.

    Delivery areas

    Six provinces, covered

    We deliver across Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland & Labrador, and Prince Edward Island. One all-in price, quoted for your exact site.

    Ontario

    Deliveries across Ontario for construction, farm, and commercial customers — from Ottawa and the east to Toronto, Hamilton, and beyond.

    Quebec

    Regular deliveries across Quebec, including the Montreal and Quebec City regions, for job sites, farms, and businesses.

    Nova Scotia

    Regular deliveries across Nova Scotia — Halifax and the mainland, Cape Breton, and everywhere in between.

    New Brunswick

    Deliveries across New Brunswick — Moncton, Saint John, Fredericton, and rural sites province-wide.

    Newfoundland & Labrador

    Deliveries arranged to Newfoundland & Labrador, coordinated with ferry schedules — ask us for timing when you request your quote.

    Prince Edward Island

    Our home base. Island-wide delivery from Charlottetown — job sites, farms, and businesses in every county, placed by a crew that knows Island roads and driveways.

    Outside the six provinces?

    Ask us — delivery further afield can often be arranged. Tell us the destination town in your quote request and we'll work out the full delivered price — container, trucking, and placement — in one number.

    The bridge factor

    Every mainland container bound for PEI crosses the Confederation Bridge, and the bridge closes to high-sided vehicles 8–12 times a winter for wind. We plan around it — and if your delivery day is one of those days, we reschedule at no extra charge.

    Why delivery is quoted per job

    Distance, site access, and bridge crossings all change the trucking cost. Rather than pad a flat rate, we quote your actual delivery — so Island customers aren't paying for someone else's long haul.
